about.title: Hi, I am Atharv.
about.body: I love to build things: websites, backend systems, AI tools, and a bit of everything in between. If it is interesting and I can make it work, I want to try it.

about.title: About me
about.body:
I am on a gap year in Khargone, Madhya Pradesh, getting ready to join Scaler School of Technology next year. I am using this time to build and learn at my own pace before college.

I run Skateflow, a skating academy that teaches waveboarding, and I take freelance web development and SEO work for local businesses. In my own time I am teaching myself the math behind AI and building Mirrors, a memory system for students.

The long-term plan is a cross-disciplinary research lab in the spirit of Bell Labs, where curiosity leads and different fields share a room. I am curious about quantum mechanics, Arduino electronics, ethical hacking, and where AI meets music and robotics.

projects.title: Mirrors
projects.summary: An AI memory and note retrieval system for students.
projects.description: Mirrors helps students retrieve useful ideas from their notes. A knowledge graph feeds the model clean, approved threads so answers stay focused.
projects.problem: Student notes and past conversations can be difficult to search, and irrelevant context can make AI answers noisy.
projects.solution: Mirrors organizes knowledge into a graph and gives the model only approved, relevant threads to answer from.

images.alt: Temporary illustrative Mirrors notes and answer interface
images.caption: Temporary concept preview

projects.journey: Mirrors began as a hackathon idea: what if students could ask questions about what they had learned and get useful answers from their own notes? The first challenge was not simply connecting a language model to stored text. Notes accumulate quickly, and giving a model too much unrelated context can make its answers less focused. I wanted the system to remember useful ideas while keeping irrelevant material out of the conversation. That question became the starting point for Mirrors, an AI memory and note retrieval system for students. I began shaping the project around a knowledge graph, so related ideas could be connected instead of treated as isolated fragments. The graph provides a way to organize a student’s knowledge and find threads that are relevant to a question. Mirrors then passes only clean, approved threads to the model. This approach is intended to make the answer more grounded in the student’s own material and reduce noise from unrelated notes. The project has grown beyond its hackathon beginning and is still in active development. I continue to work on the system’s structure and on the relationship between stored notes, retrieval, and the model’s response. Mirrors is also part of my own learning: building it lets me explore how AI tools can support students without losing sight of the information they have collected. The goal is a memory system that feels useful and dependable, where a student can return to ideas they have already explored and build on them.
